Hurghada is a Red Sea cruise port and a major coastal resort city in Eastern Egypt with population around 260,000. Hurghada is one of Egypt's main resort hubs on the Red Sea coast.

The development of the tourism industry started in the 1980s, following major domestic and foreign investments in hotels and holiday resort infrastructure, including premium watersports facilities serving popular leisure activities like windsurfing, kitesurfing, yachting, snorkeling and scuba diving. Hurghada is also well-known for its top-rated nightlife.

Hurghada Port's locode is EGHRG.

Hurghada's coastline has length approx 36 km (22 mi). As a resort vacation destination, the city is visited mainly by domestic tourists (predominantly from Egypt's capital Cairo) and also European tourists (mainly during the holidays). Hurghada is divided into 6 districts - El Ahia, El Helal, El Dahar (downtown, bazaar), Sekalla (city center), El Kawsar (the most modern) and El Memsha (a 4 km long esplanade/seafront promenade street).

As a cruise port, Hurghada was extensively included in the schedule of the superyacht Le Ponant (owned by Ponant). The luxury yacht's 2019-2020 season (December 14 through March 31) was based on roundtrip departures from homeport Aqaba (Jordan) with included overnight hotel stay in Eilat (Israel).

Prices started from ~USD 3300 per person (double-occupancy cabin rates).

On June 12, 2024, in Cairo, AD Ports Group (2006-founded as ADPC/Abu Dhabi Ports Company, Abu Dhabi UAE-based company specializing in the development and management of seaports) signed with Egypt's RSPA (Red Sea Ports Authority) a 15-year concession agreement (through 2040) for the development/operation/management of three cruise terminals (in Hurghada, Safaga, Sharm El Sheikh). By the deal, the three facilities would be upgraded and operational in 2025. By the concession deal, AD Ports Group will US$4,7 million (over the next 15 years), provide new services, enhance access for cruise shipping companies, and introduce new itineraries.

Also in 2024, AD Ports Group and SCZONE (Suez Canal Economic Zone) signed two 30-year concession agreements for a Ro-Ro ship terminal and a cruise ship terminal in Port Sokhna.
